Phase 5 is in: `run_step` now actually executes each command in the container and the graph routes on the real exit code. Nothing is simulated any more — `src/stub-exec.ts` is deleted.

## What changed in [src/graph.ts](src/graph.ts)

`run_step` calls the Docker layer's `exec` for `runnable` steps and classifies four distinct outcomes, because Phase 6 will need to tell them apart:

| outcome | status | recorded as |
|---|---|---|
| exit 0, no timeout | `pass` | advances `idx` |
| non-zero exit | `fail` | stays on `idx` for diagnose, stderr's last line logged |
| killed by the timeout | `fail` | `reason: "timed out after Ns (killed, exit 124)"` |
| stream ended with no code | `fail` | `reason: "container never reported an exit code"` |
| `exec` itself threw | `fail` | container liveness checked first; a dead container aborts with a clear message instead of failing nine steps in a row |

A killed command is no longer ambiguous with a command that legitimately exits 124: `exitCode === 0 && !timedOut` is the pass test, and the timeout case carries its own reason. `cmdCount` counts real executions only — `skip` steps (interactive/dev-server blocks) still cost nothing.

## The bug this phase exposed

The routing was subtly wrong, in a way Phase 5 is the first phase able to trigger:

```
idx = last step, command fails
  run_step → fail, idx unchanged
  routeAfterRun: last status is fail → diagnose
  diagnose advances idx past the end, returns {}
  run_step: no step → {}
  routeAfterRun: results.at(-1) is still the old fail → diagnose ...
```

Once the last step failed, the graph spun between `diagnose` and `run_step` until `RECURSION_LIMIT` (250) tripped — no error, just a silent 250-superstep burn. The fix is ordering in `routeAfterRun` ([:337](src/graph.ts#L337)): check exhaustion **before** the failure status. `diagnose` also advances `idx` without appending a result, since the failing row is already in `results` and a second identical `fail` row would only duplicate it in the report.

I also made `diagnose` honest while I was in there: the Phase 1 stub pretended `--fix` worked and wrote `workaround`. With real results, that would be a fabricated pass. It now logs `left failed; no fix attempted (phase 6)` and moves on — the graph shape is unchanged, only the lie is gone.

## Verification

`npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` clean; `dist/` rebuilt from scratch so no stale `stub-exec.js`.

A local fixture repo whose README has five real commands, `README_TEST_EXEC_TIMEOUT_MS=3000`:

```
s1 echo hello from the docs              -> pass (exit 0, 0.1s)
s2 node -e "process.exit(1)"             -> fail (exit 1, 0.4s)
s3 bash -lc 'echo boom >&2; exit 7'      -> fail (exit 7, 0.1s) — boom
s4 sleep 300                             -> fail (exit 124, 3.1s) — timed out after 3s
s5 echo still alive after the timeout     -> pass (exit 0, 0.1s)   ← container survived the kill
s6 pnpm dev                              -> skip (no exec)
cmdCount: 5   (skip excluded)
```

The `— boom` proves stderr propagation, and s5 running after s4 proves the in-container `timeout` kill leaves the sandbox usable. A second fixture with a **single failing last step** went `fail → diagnose → no step left → ci_crosscheck → report` and exited 0 — that's the routing fix under test.

Real repo, [makeplane/plane](https://github.com/makeplane/plane), 25 s per-command budget:

```
s1 git clone ... [folder-name] ⏎ cd ...   fail 124  timed out after 25s
s2 ./setup.sh                            fail 124  timed out after 25s
s3 docker compose -f ... up              fail 127  docker: command not found
s4 pnpm dev                              skip
```

Cleanup after every run: 0 containers, 0 temp clones.

## Limits

The global ~30-command cap and the resume checkpointer are Phase 9 — right now only `RECURSION_LIMIT` bounds a run. The per-command timeout is one env knob for every step, not per-step-class (a `npm install` and an `echo` share it). `s3` above also shows an environment limit worth knowing before Phase 6: the sandbox image has no Docker CLI, so any doc step that shells out to `docker` fails with 127 and a diagnose model has no honest fix available. The `exec`-threw path is coded but unexercised, since I couldn't kill a container mid-exec reliably. And the LLM path is still unverified end to end — both runs used the invalid-key fallback.

function isRootDelete(cmd: string): boolean {
  // find rm invocations
  const matches = cmd.matchAll(/\brm\s+([^;&|\n]+)/g);
  for (const m of matches) {
    const args = m[1]!.trim().split(/\s+/);
    const flags = args.filter(a => a.startsWith("-")).join("");
    const recursive = /[rR]/.test(flags) || flags.includes("--recursive");
    const targets = args.filter(a => !a.startsWith("-"));
    for (const t of targets) {
      const cleaned = t.replace(/^["']|["']$/g, "");
      if (!recursive && /^\/\*?$/.test(cleaned)) return true;
      if (/^\/(\*|$|\s)/.test(cleaned) && /[rRf]/.test(flags)) return true;
      if (/^(~|\$HOME|\/(etc|usr|bin|sbin|var|root|boot|opt|lib|lib64|proc|sys|dev))(\/|$)/.test(cleaned) && recursive) return true;
    }
  }
  return false;
}

/**
 * Commands no documented setup step needs and a hallucinating model might
 * still produce. Deliberately small: this is a guard against obvious damage,
 * not a sandbox (the container is already the sandbox).
 */
const DENY: ReadonlyArray<{ pattern: RegExp; why: string }> = [
  { pattern: /\b(mkfs(\.\w+)?|fdisk|parted|wipefs)\b/, why: "formats a block device" },
  { pattern: /\bdd\b[^|;&\n]*\bof=\/dev\//, why: "writes raw bytes to a device" },
  { pattern: /:\s*\(\s*\)\s*\{[^}]*\}\s*;\s*:/, why: "fork bomb" },
  { pattern: /\b(shutdown|reboot|halt|poweroff)\b/, why: "takes the machine down" },
  {
    pattern: /\b(curl|wget)\b[^|;&\n]*\|\s*(?:sudo\s+)?(?:ba|z|da|k)?sh\b/,
    why: "pipes a download straight into a shell",
  },
  {
    pattern: /\beval\b[^|;&\n]*\$\(\s*(curl|wget)\b/,
    why: "evaluates a downloaded script",
  },
  { pattern: /(^|[\s;&|])(sudo|doas|pkexec)\b/, why: "needs root escalation" },
  { pattern: /\bsu\s+-/, why: "needs root escalation" },
  { pattern: /\bgit\s+push\b/, why: "writes to a remote repository" },
  { pattern: /\b(npm|yarn|pnpm|bun)\s+publish\b/, why: "publishes a package" },
];

/** Directories whose recursive deletion is never a setup fix. */
const SYSTEM_PATHS = /^(~|\$HOME|\/(etc|usr|bin|sbin|var|root|boot|opt|lib|lib64|proc|sys|dev))(\/|$)/;

/**
 * Catch `rm -rf /`, `rm -rf /*`, `rm -rf ~`, `rm -rf /etc` — while letting
 * `rm -rf node_modules` and `rm -rf /workspace/dist` through, which are normal
 * setup commands.
 */
function isSystemDelete(command: string): boolean {
  for (const call of command.matchAll(/\brm\s+([^;&|\n]+)/g)) {
    const args = call[1]!.trim().split(/\s+/);
    const flags = args.filter((arg) => arg.startsWith("-")).join(" ");
    const recursive = /[rR]|--recursive/.test(flags);
    const forced = /[fF]|--force/.test(flags);
    if (!recursive || !forced) continue;

    for (const raw of args.filter((arg) => !arg.startsWith("-"))) {
      const target = raw.replace(/^["']|["']$/g, "");
      if (target === "/" || target === "/*" || target === "/.") return true;
      if (SYSTEM_PATHS.test(target)) return true;
    }
  }
  return false;
}

export interface CommandVerdict {
  allowed: boolean;
  reason?: string;
}

/**
 * Gate every model-proposed command. Checked before the container sees it, so a
 * rejection costs nothing but a log line.
 */
export function checkCommand(command: string): CommandVerdict {
  const cmd = command.trim();
  if (!cmd) return { allowed: false, reason: "empty command" };
  if (cmd.length > MAX_FIX_CHARS) {
    return { allowed: false, reason: `longer than ${MAX_FIX_CHARS} chars` };
  }

  for (const rule of DENY) {
    if (rule.pattern.test(cmd)) return { allowed: false, reason: rule.why };
  }
  if (isSystemDelete(cmd)) {
    return { allowed: false, reason: "recursive delete of the filesystem or a system directory" };
  }

  // Same heuristics the Phase 4 fallback uses: a fix that waits for stdin or
  // never exits would burn the full exec timeout and say nothing.
  if (!heuristicLabels(cmd, "", undefined).runnable) {
    return {
      allowed: false,
      reason: "would not finish unattended (interactive, long-running, or a placeholder)",
    };
  }

  return { allowed: true };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Diagnosis
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export interface Diagnosis {
  /** `workaround` only when the proposed fix really exited 0. */
  status: Extract<StepStatus, "workaround" | "fail">;
  /** The command that was run, or the one that was proposed but rejected. */
  command: string;
  exitCode: number | null;
  stdout: string;
  stderr: string;
  durationMs: number;
  reason: string;
  /** False when nothing was executed (no fix, rejected, or LLM unavailable). */
  executed: boolean;
  /** Transport/parse retries spent, added to the run's `llmRetries`. */
  llmRetries: number;
}

/** A failure that never reached the container. */
function declined(input: DiagnoseInput, reason: string, command?: string): Diagnosis {
  return {
    status: "fail",
    command: command ?? input.step.command,
    exitCode: input.failure.exitCode,
    stdout: "",
    stderr: "",
    durationMs: 0,
    reason,
    executed: false,
    llmRetries: 0,
  };
}

/**
 * Ask for one fix and try it.
 *
 * Every failure mode here is fail-soft: a rate limit, an unparseable answer, a
 * rejected command or a fix that does not work all leave the step `fail` and
 * let the run continue to the next step. Only a dead daemon is loud, and
 * `run_step` is where that is handled.
 */
export async function diagnoseStep(input: DiagnoseInput): Promise<Diagnosis> {
  const propose = input.propose ?? llmProposer();

  let fix: Fix | undefined;
  let llmRetries = 0;
  let lastError: string | undefined;

  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= 2; attempt++) {
    try {
      fix = await propose(input, attempt);
      break;
    } catch (err) {
      lastError = message(err);
      if (attempt === 1) {
        llmRetries++;
        console.warn(`[diagnose] proposal failed (${lastError}); retrying once`);
      }
    }
  }

  if (!fix) {
    return {
      ...declined(input, `diagnosis unavailable: ${lastError ?? "no answer"}`),
      llmRetries,
    };
  }

  if (fix.command === null || fix.command.trim() === "") {
    return {
      ...declined(input, `model proposed no fix: ${fix.reason.trim()}`),
      llmRetries,
    };
  }

  const proposal = fix.command.trim();
  const verdict = checkCommand(proposal);
  if (!verdict.allowed) {
    return {
      ...declined(input, `rejected unsafe fix (${verdict.reason}): ${proposal}`, proposal),
      llmRetries,
    };
  }

  if (flat(proposal) === flat(input.step.command)) {
    return {
      ...declined(input, "model returned the failing command unchanged", proposal),
      llmRetries,
    };
  }

  let out: ExecResult;
  try {
    out = await exec(input.containerId, proposal, { timeoutMs: input.timeoutMs });
  } catch (err) {
    return {
      ...declined(input, `could not run the fix: ${message(err)}`, proposal),
      llmRetries,
    };
  }

  const worked = out.exitCode === 0 && !out.timedOut;
  const note = fix.reason.trim();

  return {
    status: worked ? "workaround" : "fail",
    command: proposal,
    exitCode: out.exitCode,
    stdout: out.stdout,
    stderr: out.stderr,
    durationMs: out.durationMs,
    reason: worked
      ? note
      : out.timedOut
        ? `${note} — the fix timed out after ${Math.round(out.durationMs / 1000)}s`
        : `${note} — the fix failed too (exit ${out.exitCode ?? "?"})`,
    executed: true,
    llmRetries,
  };
}

Phase 6 is in: [src/diagnose.ts](src/diagnose.ts) asks the strong model for one structured fix, gates it, runs it once, and the graph records `workaround` or `fail`.

## The fix contract

```ts
{ command: string | null, reason: string }
```

`null` is a first-class answer, not a parse failure. On Plane every failing step fails for a reason no in-container command can repair (no Docker daemon, a 98 MB re-clone timing out), and forcing a command there produces a plausible-looking fix that fails immediately and teaches the report nothing. So the prompt says plainly: if it can't be fixed from inside the container, return `null` and explain why.

The prompt carries the failing command, its doc path and heading, the exit code, and **both** truncated output streams — `exec` already caps each at the last 2 KB, which is exactly the budget the plan asked for. It also states the environment limits that make fixes realistic: root, non-interactive, no TTY, no Docker daemon, no sudo, repo at `/workspace`.

## The denylist

Small on purpose — the container is already the sandbox, this only stops obvious damage:

`rm -rf /` `/*` `~` `/etc` (and `/usr`, `/var`, `/root`, …) · `mkfs`/`fdisk`/`parted` · `dd of=/dev/…` · fork bombs · `shutdown`/`reboot` · `curl … | sh` · `eval $(curl …)` · `sudo`/`doas`/`pkexec`/`su -` · `git push` · `npm|yarn|pnpm publish`

The `rm` rule is parsed rather than regex-matched on the whole line, because the naive version also blocks the most common legitimate fix: `rm -rf node_modules && npm install` and `rm -rf /workspace/dist` pass, `rm -rf /` does not. A second gate reuses Phase 4's `heuristicLabels`, so a fix that waits on stdin or never exits (`npm run dev`) is rejected instead of burning a full exec timeout.

Every rejection names its reason in the report — `rejected unsafe fix (takes the machine down): shutdown -h now` — and costs **zero** commands, since nothing reached the container.

## Behaviour on each path

| situation | status | command budget |
|---|---|---|
| fix exits 0 | `workaround`, with the model's reason | +1 |
| fix exits non-zero | `fail`, reason says "the fix failed too (exit 3)" | +1 |
| model returns `null` | `fail`, model's explanation surfaced | 0 |
| fix rejected by denylist | `fail`, reason + the rejected command shown | 0 |
| fix identical to the failing command | `fail` — no point re-running it | 0 |
| LLM 401/429/parse error | one retry, then `fail` with "diagnosis unavailable" | 0 |

That last row is the important one: diagnosis is best-effort, so a provider outage degrades a single step instead of aborting a run that already has results.

`npm run typecheck` / `npm run build` clean. A scratch script (deleted) ran **61 checks, 61 passing**, against a real container:

- 15 denied commands each rejected with the right reason; 7 legitimate ones allowed, including both `rm -rf node_modules && npm install` and `rm -rf /workspace/dist`
- 6 prompt assertions (command, stderr, exit code, doc source, "never start a server", `command=null`)

+/**
+ * Phase 6: diagnose a failed step.
+ *
+ * Input is the failing command plus the truncated stderr/stdout the Docker
+ * layer already captured. The strong model proposes one fix as structured
+ * output; we run it once. A fix that works turns the step into `workaround`,
+ * anything else leaves it `fail`.
+ *
+ * The model never gets to run a command unchecked: `checkCommand` rejects
+ * destructive, privileged, publishing and non-terminating commands before
+ * anything reaches the container.
+ */
+import { z } from "zod";
+import { exec, type ExecResult } from "./docker.js";
+import { heuristicLabels } from "./docs.js";
+import { getStrong } from "./llm.js";
+import type { Step, StepResult, StepStatus } from "./state.js";
+
+/** A proposed fix must be a command, not an essay. */
+const MAX_FIX_CHARS = 2000;
+
+/**
+ * What the model may answer.
+ *
+ * `command: null` is a real answer, not a failure: plenty of documented steps
+ * fail for reasons no in-container command can fix (no Docker daemon, no
+ * credentials, the docs are simply wrong), and saying so is more useful than
+ * inventing a plausible-looking command that fails too.
+ */
+export const FixSchema = z.object({
+  command: z
+    .string()
+    .nullable()
+    .describe(
+      "One shell command that should make the failed step succeed, run from the repo root. " +
+        "null when no command-level fix is honest.",
+    ),
+  reason: z
+    .string()
+    .describe("One or two sentences: why the documented command failed, and what the fix changes."),
+});
+export type Fix = z.infer<typeof FixSchema>;
+
+/** Test seam: same shape as the extract classifier's injected model call. */
+export type Proposer = (input: DiagnoseInput, attempt: number) => Promise<Fix>;
+
+const message = (err: unknown): string => (err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err));
+
+const flat = (command: string): string => command.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
+
+/**
+ * Reasons end up in the report, so keep them to one readable line: a provider
+ * error body is a wall of JSON and a stack trace is worse.
+ */
+function brief(text: string, max = 220): string {
+  const oneLine = text.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
+  return oneLine.length > max ? `${oneLine.slice(0, max)}…` : oneLine;
+}
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// Prompt
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+export interface DiagnoseInput {
+  containerId: string;
+  step: Step;
+  /** The failing row `run_step` appended. Its stderr is the whole diagnosis. */
+  failure: StepResult;
+  image?: string;
+  timeoutMs?: number;
+  propose?: Proposer;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Build the diagnosis prompt.
+ *
+ * stdout and stderr are already truncated to the last ~2 KB by `exec`, which is
+ * exactly the budget the plan specifies. Both are included: plenty of tools
+ * print the cause on stdout and only stack frames on stderr.
+ */
+export function buildFixPrompt(input: DiagnoseInput): string {
+  const { step, failure } = input;
+  const stdout = failure.stdout.trim() || "(empty)";
+  const stderr = failure.stderr.trim() || "(empty)";
+
+  return `A documented setup command failed in a clean container while auditing a repository's instructions.
+
+Environment:
+- The repository is cloned at /workspace; this command runs there.
+- Image: ${input.image ?? "node:22-bookworm"}, running as root, non-interactive, no TTY.
+- Bash is available. No Docker daemon, no sudo, no browser, no credentials.
+
+Rules:
+1. Propose ONE command that makes the documented step succeed. It must exit on its own — never start a server, watcher or interactive session.
+2. Keep the documented intent: fix the install, do not skip it or stub it out.
+3. Prefer the smallest honest fix: a missing system package, the repository's real install command (npm ci, pnpm install --frozen-lockfile), a flag the docs omit.
+4. Do not return the failing command unchanged.
+5. If the failure cannot be fixed from inside the container, return command=null and explain why.
+
+Failed step:
+  command: ${step.command.replace(/\n/g, "\n           ")}
+  source: ${step.source}${step.heading ? ` (section: ${step.heading})` : ""}
+  exit code: ${failure.exitCode ?? "unknown"}
+
+stdout (last ~2 KB):
+${stdout}
+
+stderr (last ~2 KB):
+${stderr}`;
+}
+
+/** The production proposer: one structured call to the strong model. */
+function llmProposer(): Proposer {
+  const structured = getStrong().withStructuredOutput(FixSchema, { name: "propose_setup_fix" });
+  return async (input) => FixSchema.parse(await structured.invoke(buildFixPrompt(input)));
+}
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// Denylist
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+/**
+ * Commands no documented setup step needs and a hallucinating model might
+ * still produce. Deliberately small: this is a guard against obvious damage,
+ * not a sandbox (the container is already the sandbox).
+ */
+const DENY: ReadonlyArray<{ pattern: RegExp; why: string }> = [
+  { pattern: /\b(mkfs(\.\w+)?|fdisk|parted|wipefs)\b/, why: "formats a block device" },
+  { pattern: /\bdd\b[^|;&\n]*\bof=\/dev\//, why: "writes raw bytes to a device" },
+  { pattern: /:\s*\(\s*\)\s*\{[^}]*\}\s*;\s*:/, why: "fork bomb" },
+  { pattern: /\b(shutdown|reboot|halt|poweroff)\b/, why: "takes the machine down" },
+  {
+    pattern: /\b(curl|wget)\b[^|;&\n]*\|\s*(?:sudo\s+)?(?:ba|z|da|k)?sh\b/,
+    why: "pipes a download straight into a shell",
+  },
+  {
+    pattern: /\beval\b[^|;&\n]*\$\(\s*(curl|wget)\b/,
+    why: "evaluates a downloaded script",
+  },
+  { pattern: /(^|[\s;&|])(sudo|doas|pkexec)\b/, why: "needs root escalation" },
+  { pattern: /\bsu\s+-/, why: "needs root escalation" },
+  { pattern: /\bgit\s+push\b/, why: "writes to a remote repository" },
+  { pattern: /\b(npm|yarn|pnpm|bun)\s+publish\b/, why: "publishes a package" },
+];
+
+/** Directories whose recursive deletion is never a setup fix. */
+const SYSTEM_PATHS = /^(~|\$HOME|\/(etc|usr|bin|sbin|var|root|boot|opt|lib|lib64|proc|sys|dev))(\/|$)/;
+
+/**
+ * Catch `rm -rf /`, `rm -rf /*`, `rm -rf ~`, `rm -rf /etc` — while letting
+ * `rm -rf node_modules` and `rm -rf /workspace/dist` through, which are normal
+ * setup commands.
+ */
+function isSystemDelete(command: string): boolean {
+  for (const call of command.matchAll(/\brm\s+([^;&|\n]+)/g)) {
+    const args = call[1]!.trim().split(/\s+/);
+    const flags = args.filter((arg) => arg.startsWith("-")).join(" ");
+    const recursive = /[rR]|--recursive/.test(flags);
+    const forced = /[fF]|--force/.test(flags);
+    if (!recursive || !forced) continue;
+
+    for (const raw of args.filter((arg) => !arg.startsWith("-"))) {
+      const target = raw.replace(/^["']|["']$/g, "");
+      if (target === "/" || target === "/*" || target === "/.") return true;
+      if (SYSTEM_PATHS.test(target)) return true;
+    }
+  }
+  return false;
+}
+
+export interface CommandVerdict {
+  allowed: boolean;
+  reason?: string;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Gate every model-proposed command. Checked before the container sees it, so a
+ * rejection costs nothing but a log line.
+ */
+export function checkCommand(command: string): CommandVerdict {
+  const cmd = command.trim();
+  if (!cmd) return { allowed: false, reason: "empty command" };
+  if (cmd.length > MAX_FIX_CHARS) {
+    return { allowed: false, reason: `longer than ${MAX_FIX_CHARS} chars` };
+  }
+
+  for (const rule of DENY) {
+    if (rule.pattern.test(cmd)) return { allowed: false, reason: rule.why };
+  }
+  if (isSystemDelete(cmd)) {
+    return { allowed: false, reason: "recursive delete of the filesystem or a system directory" };
+  }
+
+  // Same heuristics the Phase 4 fallback uses: a fix that waits for stdin or
+  // never exits would burn the full exec timeout and say nothing.
+  if (!heuristicLabels(cmd, "", undefined).runnable) {
+    return {
+      allowed: false,
+      reason: "would not finish unattended (interactive, long-running, or a placeholder)",
+    };
+  }
+
+  return { allowed: true };
+}
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// Diagnosis
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+export interface Diagnosis {
+  /** `workaround` only when the proposed fix really exited 0. */
+  status: Extract<StepStatus, "workaround" | "fail">;
+  /** The command that was run, or the one that was proposed but rejected. */
+  command: string;
+  exitCode: number | null;
+  stdout: string;
+  stderr: string;
+  durationMs: number;
+  reason: string;
+  /** False when nothing was executed (no fix, rejected, or LLM unavailable). */
+  executed: boolean;
+  /** Transport/parse retries spent, added to the run's `llmRetries`. */
+  llmRetries: number;
+}
+
+/** A failure that never reached the container. */
+function declined(input: DiagnoseInput, reason: string, command?: string): Diagnosis {
+  return {
+    status: "fail",
+    command: command ?? input.step.command,
+    exitCode: input.failure.exitCode,
+    stdout: "",
+    stderr: "",
+    durationMs: 0,
+    reason,
+    executed: false,
+    llmRetries: 0,
+  };
+}
+
+/**
+ * Ask for one fix and try it.
+ *
+ * Every failure mode here is fail-soft: a rate limit, an unparseable answer, a
+ * rejected command or a fix that does not work all leave the step `fail` and
+ * let the run continue to the next step. Only a dead daemon is loud, and
+ * `run_step` is where that is handled.
+ */
+export async function diagnoseStep(input: DiagnoseInput): Promise<Diagnosis> {
+  const propose = input.propose ?? llmProposer();
+
+  let fix: Fix | undefined;
+  let llmRetries = 0;
+  let lastError: string | undefined;
+
+  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= 2; attempt++) {
+    try {
+      fix = await propose(input, attempt);
+      break;
+    } catch (err) {
+      lastError = message(err);
+      if (attempt === 1) {
+        llmRetries++;
+        console.warn(`[diagnose] proposal failed (${lastError}); retrying once`);
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  if (!fix) {
+    return {
+      ...declined(input, `diagnosis unavailable: ${brief(lastError ?? "no answer")}`),
+      llmRetries,
+    };
+  }
+
+  if (fix.command === null || fix.command.trim() === "") {
+    return {
+      ...declined(input, `model proposed no fix: ${brief(fix.reason)}`),
+      llmRetries,
+    };
+  }
+
+  const proposal = fix.command.trim();
+  const verdict = checkCommand(proposal);
+  if (!verdict.allowed) {
+    return {
+      ...declined(input, `rejected unsafe fix (${verdict.reason}): ${proposal}`, proposal),
+      llmRetries,
+    };
+  }
+
+  if (flat(proposal) === flat(input.step.command)) {
+    return {
+      ...declined(input, "model returned the failing command unchanged", proposal),
+      llmRetries,
+    };
+  }
+
+  let out: ExecResult;
+  try {
+    out = await exec(input.containerId, proposal, { timeoutMs: input.timeoutMs });
+  } catch (err) {
+    return {
+      ...declined(input, `could not run the fix: ${message(err)}`, proposal),
+      llmRetries,
+    };
+  }
+
+  const worked = out.exitCode === 0 && !out.timedOut;
+  const note = brief(fix.reason);
+
+  return {
+    status: worked ? "workaround" : "fail",
+    command: proposal,
+    exitCode: out.exitCode,
+    stdout: out.stdout,
+    stderr: out.stderr,
+    durationMs: out.durationMs,
+    reason: worked
+      ? note
+      : out.timedOut
+        ? `${note} — the fix timed out after ${Math.round(out.durationMs / 1000)}s`
+        : `${note} — the fix failed too (exit ${out.exitCode ?? "?"})`,
+    executed: true,
+    llmRetries,
+  };
+}

Your key works, and it immediately paid for itself: the first real-model run exposed two bugs that no stubbed test could have found. Both are fixed.

## 1. LLM extraction (Phase 4) — happy path confirmed

Fixture README with four shell blocks (install, a Yarn alternative, `jq --version`, `npm run dev`) plus a JS block:

```
[extract_steps] model answer: 3 label(s), 0 unknown id(s), 0 duplicate(s), ~1 block(s) not labelled
[extract_steps] 3 step(s) from 4 block(s): 2 runnable, 1 not (skipped), LLM ordered
```

It dropped the Yarn alternative as a duplicate (rule 2), kept doc order, and labelled `npm run dev` not runnable. On Plane it did the thing the heuristics never could: `docker compose -f docker-compose-local.yml up` → **skip**, in all three runs.

## 2. Phase 6 — a real fix, verified

`jq` is genuinely absent from `node:22-bookworm`, so `jq --version` failed with 127:

```
[diagnose] s1 -> workaround (tried `apt-get update && apt-get install -y jq`, 2 command(s))
```

`npm install left-pad` then passed, `npm run dev` skipped, `cmdCount: 4`.

## The bug the first Plane run found

The model proposed `apt-get install git` — git *is* installed; the clone had been killed by the 25 s timeout. That command exited 0, and the tool called the step a **workaround** without ever re-running `git clone`. A fix exiting 0 proves nothing.

`diagnoseStep` now re-runs the documented command after a fix succeeds (one extra command), and `workaround` means the step genuinely passes:

| fix outcome | status | commands |
|---|---|---|
| fix fails | `fail` | 1 |
| fix exits 0, documented command passes | `workaround` | 2 |
| fix exits 0, documented command still fails | `fail`, reason names the still-failing step | 2 |

Same Plane step before and after:

```
before:  workaround via `apt-get update && apt-get install -y git`
after:   fail  — the fix exited 0, but the documented command still fails (exit 124)
```

On Plane the new row reports the *documented* command with exit 124, and names the attempted fix in the note, so the table no longer claims work that didn't happen.

## The bug that caused the bad guess

The prompt listed `exit code: 124` but not the runner's own note, so the model read "fetch-pack: unexpected disconnect" and blamed git. `buildFixPrompt` now includes it:

```
  runner note: timed out after 25s (killed, exit 124) (the sandbox runner, not the command itself)
```

The next Plane run proposed `git clone --depth 1 …` — the correct mitigation for a slow clone. It still exceeded 25 s on this connection and was reported as a timeout rather than dressed up as a fix. The second failure (`./setup.sh` + corepack) produced `npm i -g pnpm@11.10.0 && corepack enable && ./setup.sh`, exit 1 → honest `fail`.

I also fixed the log wording: it said "via" the documented command when the command actually run was the fix. It now reads `(tried \`<fix>\`, N command(s))`.

## What I verified

`npm run typecheck` / `npm run build` clean after every edit. A scratch script (deleted) ran **16/16** against a real container: re-verified fix → `workaround` (2 commands, exit 0 from the re-run); irrelevant fix → `fail` with `still fails (exit 1)`; failing fix → 1 command only; `rm -rf /` → 0 commands, workspace intact. Plus three real end-to-end runs with your key (fixture twice, Plane twice) and zero leftover containers or clones.

## Worth knowing

**Labelling is not deterministic.** Three Plane runs with identical prompts and `temperature: 0` gave 3, 2 and 2 runnable steps — `./setup.sh` was skipped in one run and executed in the next. The report is a sample of the model's judgement, not a fixed answer.

**Re-verification costs a command per successful-looking fix**, so a run with many diagnosed steps spends more of the ~30-command budget Phase 9 will enforce.

**The `[folder-name]` block is still labelled runnable** by the model, so it re-clones the repo inside the container — the placeholder gap from the Phase 4 review is still the one to fix. The report also still shows two rows per failed step until Phase 8 collapses them.

export function collapseResults(steps: Step[], results: StepResult[]): StepOutcome[] {
  const byId = new Map<string, StepResult[]>();
  for (const r of results) {
    const list = byId.get(r.stepId) ?? [];
    list.push(r);
    byId.set(r.stepId, list);

  return steps.map(step => {
    const rows = byId.get(step.stepId) ?? [];
    const [attempt, diagnosis] = rows;
    const final = rows.at(-1);
    return { step, ...(attempt?{attempt}:{}), ...(diagnosis?{diagnosis}:{}), status: final?.status ?? "not_run", ...(final?{final}:{}) };
  });
}

export function excerpt(text: string, maxLines = 12, maxChars = 1200): string {
  const lines = text.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n").trimEnd().split("\n");
  if (lines.length === 0 || (lines.length === 1 && lines[0] === "")) return "";
  let kept = lines.slice(-maxLines);
  let truncated = kept.length < lines.length;
  let body = kept.join("\n");
  if (body.length > maxChars) { body = body.slice(-maxChars); truncated = true; }
  return truncated ? `…\n${body}` : body;
}

function findRange(lines: string[], command: string): { start: number; end: number } | undefined {
  const target = command.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n").split("\n").map(l => l.trimEnd());
  // drop leading/trailing empties
  while (target.length && target[0]!.trim() === "") target.shift();
  while (target.length && target.at(-1)!.trim() === "") target.pop();
  if (target.length === 0) return undefined;

  const normalizedTarget = target.map(norm);
  for (let i = 0; i + target.length <= lines.length; i++) {
    let ok = true;
    for (let k = 0; k < target.length; k++) {
      if (norm(lines[i + k]!) !== normalizedTarget[k]) { ok = false; break; }
    }
    if (ok) return { start: i, end: i + target.length };
  }
  return undefined;
}
```

const CONTEXT = 3;

function formatRange(start: number, count: number): string {
  return count <= 1 ? `${start + 1}` : `${start + 1},${count}`;
}

function buildDiff(path: string, lines: string[], start: number, end: number, replacement: string[]): string {
  const from = Math.max(0, start - CONTEXT);
  const to = Math.min(lines.length, end + CONTEXT);
  const before = lines.slice(from, start);
  const removed = lines.slice(start, end);
  const after = lines.slice(end, to);
  const oldCount = before.length + removed.length + after.length;
  const newCount = before.length + replacement.length + after.length;

  const oldRange = oldCount === 0 ? `${from},0` : formatRange(from, oldCount);
  const newRange = formatRange(from, newCount);
  const body = [
    ...before.map(l => ` ${l}`),
    ...removed.map(l => `-${l}`),
    ...replacement.map(l => `+${l}`),
    ...after.map(l => ` ${l}`),
  ];
  return [`--- a/${path}`, `+++ b/${path}`, `@@ -${oldRange} +${newRange} @@`, ...body].join("\n");
}

export async function writePatchNotes(input: NoteInput, opts: { write?: NoteWriter } = {}): Promise<{ notes: Record<string,string>; llmRetries: number }> {
  if (input.failures.length === 0) return { notes: {}, llmRetries: 0 };
  const write = opts.write ?? llmNoteWriter();
  let lastError;
  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= 2; attempt++) {
    try {
      const answer = await write(input, attempt);
      const ids = new Set(input.failures.map(f => f.step.id));
      const notes: Record<string,string> = {};
      let dropped = 0;
      for (const item of answer.notes) {
        if (!ids.has(item.stepId)) { dropped++; continue; }
        const note = brief(item.note, 240);
        if (note) notes[item.stepId] = note;
      }
      if (dropped > 0) console.warn(`[report] ignored ${dropped} patch note(s) with an unknown step id`);
      return { notes, llmRetries: attempt - 1 };
    } catch (err) { lastError = message(err); if (attempt===1) console.warn(...); }
  }
  console.warn(`[report] patch wording unavailable (...); using deterministic notes`);
  return { notes: {}, llmRetries: 1 };
}

 * One row per step, using its final result.

export function finalResults(results: StepResult[]): StepResult[] {
  const order: string[] = [];
  const byStep = new Map<string, StepResult>();

  const hasOutput = (result: StepResult): boolean =>
    result.stderr.trim() !== "" || result.stdout.trim() !== "";

  for (const result of results) {
    const previous = byStep.get(result.stepId);
    if (!previous) {
      order.push(result.stepId);
      byStep.set(result.stepId, result);
      continue;
    }

    const merged: StepResult = {
      ...result,
      stdout: hasOutput(result) ? result.stdout : previous.stdout,
      stderr: hasOutput(result) ? result.stderr : previous.stderr,
      durationMs: previous.durationMs + result.durationMs,
    };
    byStep.set(result.stepId, merged);
  }

  return order.map((stepId) => byStep.get(stepId)!);
}

Phase 8 is done: the report is real, and `readme-test` is a working CLI. All of it was exercised against a Docker-backed fixture repo, not just typechecked.

## What the report contains

**[src/report.ts](src/report.ts)** (new) — `buildReport` is pure, templated markdown, one row per step:

- **Summary** — pass / workaround / fail / skip counts, commands executed, retries spent, patches suggested.
- **Steps table** — command, status, exit code, duration, and the doc file plus heading the step came from.
- **Failures** — per failed step: source, command, exit code, duration, and a note. Under it, a fenced excerpt of the last 12 meaningful lines of stderr (stdout when stderr is empty), capped at 1400 chars, ANSI-stripped, with a leading `…` when the head was cut so the block never pretends to start at the top.
- **Suggested README patch** — a real `diff` fence plus one or two sentences of wording.
- **CI cross-check** — the Phase 7 summary and findings table, moved out of the graph stub.

The model (`suggestPatchWording`) writes only the prose under each patch, one structured call with one retry. Every patch's `- old / + new` pair is decided in code, and a failed call falls back to the diagnosis sentence, so a 429 costs wording and nothing else. Error excerpts are code, never model output.

## Three bugs the real runs exposed

**1. Diagnosed steps were rendered twice.** `run_step` records a `fail` and `diagnose` records the outcome for the same step, so the report had two identical failure sections, a doubled table row, and a footer claiming "5 steps failing" over a 4-step run. `finalResults` now collapses per step: last result wins, durations sum, and the earlier documented-command output is kept when the diagnosis never touched the container.

**2. A workaround is not always a replacement.** The model often fixes a doc command with a *prerequisite* (`npm install --save-dev typescript` so `npm run build` works). Rendering that as a one-for-one swap would tell a maintainer to delete the command that actually works. `patchKind` reuses Phase 7's `actionOf`: same action → replacement; different action → the patch adds a `+` line above the documented command and leaves it intact. A redundant `sh -c "…"` wrapper around a fix is unwrapped in the patch, since a doc fence already runs in a shell.

**3. Unlabelled doc blocks produced false CI findings.** The classifier labelled 2 of 6 blocks on one run, and because `docCommands` was built from labelled blocks only, the diff reported "CI tests, the docs don't mention it" for commands the README plainly contains. `documented` now comes from every extracted shell block in doc order — whether a command is in the docs is a fact, not a model decision. The same fixture's CI section went from three findings (two false) to the one real mismatch.

I also renamed the failure line from "Problem" to "Note": that text is the model's reading of the failure or a runner timeout note, while the exit code and the quoted output are the evidence.

## CLI

**[src/index.ts](src/index.ts)** — `readme-test <url> --mode user|contributor`, `-h/--help`, unknown-option and bad-mode errors, report to stdout after the progress log. **[package.json](package.json)** now declares `"bin": { "readme-test": "dist/index.js" }`, and the built file carries its shebang.

## Verification

`npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` clean. A scratch suite (deleted) ran **37 checks, 37 passing**, covering excerpt tail/ANSI/line-and-char caps, `keyErrorLine`, patch planning and dedupe, replace-vs-prerequisite classification, shell unwrapping, wording retry/fail-soft and unknown-step filtering, per-step collapsing, and full-report rendering cases (nothing to run, nothing patchable, pipes in cells, backticks inside a fence needing a longer fence, determinism, single trailing newline).

The real runs used a fixture repo whose README documents `npm ci` without a lockfile and an eslint script with eslint missing. The final run produced a report with 4 step rows, 1 workaround, 2 failures with genuine excerpts, one patch (`- npm ci / + npm install && npm ci`) with model wording, and one CI mismatch; the container was destroyed at the end. `node dist/index.js --help` and the bad-`--mode` path both behave.

Limitations worth knowing: nothing is committed; `src/ci.ts` and `src/report.ts` are untracked and `src/extract.ts`, `src/graph.ts`, `src/index.ts`, `src/state.ts`, `package.json` are modified. A `fail` step gets an explanation and no diff — that is deliberate, since there is no verified command to substitute. Patches are suggestions in the report; nothing edits a README. And the report is only as complete as Phase 4's extraction: when the classifier skips a block, that step is not run (though it now still counts as documented for the CI diff).

Progress note:
Phase 8 is done: the report is real, and `readme-test` is a working CLI. All of it was exercised against a Docker-backed fixture repo, not just typechecked.

## What the report contains

**[src/report.ts](src/report.ts)** (new) — `buildReport` is pure, templated markdown, one row per step:

- **Summary** — pass / workaround / fail / skip counts, commands executed, retries spent, patches suggested.
- **Steps table** — command, status, exit code, duration, and the doc file plus heading the step came from.
- **Failures** — per failed step: source, command, exit code, duration, and a note. Under it, a fenced excerpt of the last 12 meaningful lines of stderr (stdout when stderr is empty), capped at 1400 chars, ANSI-stripped, with a leading `…` when the head was cut so the block never pretends to start at the top.
- **Suggested README patch** — a real `diff` fence plus one or two sentences of wording.
- **CI cross-check** — the Phase 7 summary and findings table, moved out of the graph stub.

The model (`suggestPatchWording`) writes only the prose under each patch, one structured call with one retry. Every patch's `- old / + new` pair is decided in code, and a failed call falls back to the diagnosis sentence, so a 429 costs wording and nothing else. Error excerpts are code, never model output.

## Three bugs the real runs exposed

**1. Diagnosed steps were rendered twice.** `run_step` records a `fail` and `diagnose` records the outcome for the same step, so the report had two identical failure sections, a doubled table row, and a footer claiming "5 steps failing" over a 4-step run. `finalResults` now collapses per step: last result wins, durations sum, and the earlier documented-command output is kept when the diagnosis never touched the container.

**2. A workaround is not always a replacement.** The model often fixes a doc command with a *prerequisite* (`npm install --save-dev typescript` so `npm run build` works). Rendering that as a one-for-one swap would tell a maintainer to delete the command that actually works. `patchKind` reuses Phase 7's `actionOf`: same action → replacement; different action → the patch adds a `+` line above the documented command and leaves it intact. A redundant `sh -c "…"` wrapper around a fix is unwrapped in the patch, since a doc fence already runs in a shell.

**3. Unlabelled doc blocks produced false CI findings.** The classifier labelled 2 of 6 blocks on one run, and because `docCommands` was built from labelled blocks only, the diff reported "CI tests, the docs don't mention it" for commands the README plainly contains. `documented` now comes from every extracted shell block in doc order — whether a command is in the docs is a fact, not a model decision. The same fixture's CI section went from three findings (two false) to the one real mismatch.

I also renamed the failure line from "Problem" to "Note": that text is the model's reading of the failure or a runner timeout note, while the exit code and the quoted output are the evidence.

/**
 * Phase 3, host side: get the repo onto disk.
 *
 * The clone happens on the host (git is installed there; the container only
 * needs a bind mount) into a temp directory that is removed when the run ends.
 *
 * Workdirs created here are tracked so `removeAllWorkdirs()` can clean up after
 * a crash — including when the graph throws instead of reaching `report`.
 */
import { execFile } from "node:child_process";
import { mkdtemp, rm } from "node:fs/promises";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";
import { promisify } from "node:util";

const run = promisify(execFile);

/** Directory name of the clone inside the temp workdir. */
export const CLONE_DIR_NAME = "repo";

/** A slow repo (monorepo, shallow clone) can still take a while. */
export const DEFAULT_CLONE_TIMEOUT_MS = Number(

Both remaining phases are in: Phase 9 is fully implemented and verified, and Phase 10 ran against five real repositories, which turned up four bugs worth fixing.

## Phase 9: rate limits, budgets, checkpoints

**[src/llm.ts](src/llm.ts)** now owns every model call through `callModel(what, fn)`:

- Exponential backoff with 75–125% jitter (2s → 60s), logging `[llm] waiting on rate limit — extract_steps, retry 2/5 in 3.6s`. A silent 40-second pause is indistinguishable from a hang, so the line is the feature.
- 429 detection that walks `cause`, `error` and `response`, and recognises Groq's `rate_limit_exceeded` code as well as status 429 and "tokens per minute"/quota text. 5xx and dropped sockets are retried on the same schedule; validation errors are not.
- A call budget (`README_TEST_MAX_LLM_CALLS`, default 60) counted per attempt, retries included. Past it, `callModel` throws `LlmBudgetExhausted` without reaching the provider, so extraction falls back to heuristics, diagnosis declines, the CI summary stays empty and the patch keeps its fallback sentence — the report still comes out, it just says less.
- `maxRetries: 0` on the Groq clients, so retries are ours to log and count instead of the SDK's invisible ones.

**Commands** are capped at 30 (`README_TEST_MAX_COMMANDS`). `run_step` stops executing at the cap and records every remaining step as `skip` with the reason, so the report accounts for the whole docs set instead of quietly shortening. `diagnose` needs two commands of headroom (fix plus verification) and otherwise leaves the failure as recorded — a `workaround` nobody re-ran is exactly the claim this tool exists to avoid.

**Checkpoints**: `buildGraph` compiles with a `MemorySaver`, the CLI prints a run id and accepts `--thread`, and **[src/run.ts](src/run.ts)** holds the resume policy — up to two retries on a rate limit, 5s+ backoff, in-process. The container is still destroyed in the CLI's `finally`.

### The resume bug that mattered

My first pass re-invoked with the original input. A small checkpointer test showed why that is wrong: LangGraph treats an input object as a *new run* and starts at `START` again, while `null` resumes the pending superstep. So the "resume" would have re-cloned the repo, started a second container and re-run every step that had already passed. `invokeWithResume` now passes `input` on the first attempt and `null` afterwards, and there is a test asserting exactly that (`[runInput, null]`, one sleep).

The report credited rejected fixes to the docs.** Look at steps s3 and s4: the "Command" column showed `bash -c "curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash …"` and `apt-get update && …`, while the error excerpt underneath was `bash: line 4: bun: command not found` — output from the *documented* command. The docs never contain curl. Cause: `declined()` in [diagnose.ts](src/diagnose.ts) returned the model's proposal as `command`. Now the proposal goes in a separate `attemptedFix` field, shown as its own **Attempted fix** line, and `command` is always the documented one.

A documented `git clone` burned two minutes and produced a false failure.** s1 cloned ParadevAI/Paradev *again*, inside the container, from a repo the tool had already cloned — exit 137 after 125.1s. [extract.ts](src/extract.ts) now recognises a block that is nothing but a clone-of-this-repo (`git clone [flags] <url>` plus `cd`, in URL/scp/`owner/repo` form) and records it as a skip with a specific reason. Clone of a *different* repo still runs, and a block that clones then does real work is left alone.

**3. [graph.ts](src/graph.ts) now routes `diagnose` on `idx` alone. **4. The CI summary was cut mid-sentence** — "…meaning the build process described in the docs does no…". [ci.ts](src/ci.ts) clamped model prose at 600 chars. Prose is now trimmed at a sentence boundary, so the paragraph reads as a paragraph.

**5. `npm run format` in a Bun repo.** [ci.ts](src/ci.ts) hardcoded `npm run <script>` for package.json findings. It now derives the manager from the `packageManager` field or the lockfile (`bun.lockb`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`).

import { buildReport } from "./dist/report.js";

let failures = 0;
const check = (label, ok, detail = "") => {
  console.log(`${ok ? "ok  " : "FAIL"}  ${label}${detail ? ` — ${detail}` : ""}`);
  if (!ok) failures++;
};

/** Rendered text of every code span on a line. */
function spans(line) {
  const out = [];
  let i = 0;
  while (i < line.length) {
    if (line[i] !== "`") {
      i++;
      continue;
    }
    let n = 0;
    while (line[i + n] === "`") n++;
    const open = i;
    let j = i + n;
    let close = -1;
    while (j < line.length) {
      if (line[j] === "`") {
        let m = 0;
        while (line[j + m] === "`") m++;
        if (m === n) {
          close = j;
          break;
        }
        j += m;
      } else j++;
    }
    if (close === -1) {
      out.push({ text: null, raw: line.slice(open) });
      i = open + n;
      continue;
    }
    let text = line.slice(open + n, close).replace(/\n/g, " ");
    if (text.startsWith(" ") && text.endsWith(" ") && text.trim() !== "") text = text.slice(1, -1);
    out.push({ text, raw: line.slice(open, close + n) });
    i = close + n;
  }
  return out;
}

/** Split a table row on unescaped pipes; unescape the cell content. */
function cells(row) {
  const body = row.replace(/^\|/, "").replace(/\|$/, "");
  const out = [];
  let cell = "";
  for (let i = 0; i < body.length; i++) {
    const ch = body[i];
    if (ch === "\\" && body[i + 1] === "|") {
      cell += "|";
      i++;
    } else if (ch === "|") {
      out.push(cell);
      cell = "";
    } else cell += ch;
  }
  out.push(cell);
  return out;
}

+/**
+ * Markdown helpers shared by the report (Phase 8) and the CI notes (Phase 7).
+ *
+ * Both put repository content — a documented command, the command CI actually
+ * runs — inside inline code, and that content is arbitrary. A documented step
+ * like "bun run lint  # Run `bun run lint:fix` first" is ordinary, and it breaks
+ * a single-backtick code span: the span closes at the inner backtick and the
+ * rest of the command spills into the cell as prose. The rule for surviving
+ * this lives here so both call sites cannot disagree about it.
+ */
+
+/**
+ * Wrap text in an inline code span that survives backticks inside it.
+ *
+ * The delimiter is a run longer than any run in the text, the same rule a
+ * fenced block uses. When the content itself starts or ends with a backtick,
+ * one space is added at each end — otherwise that backtick would merge with the
+ * delimiter into a longer run — and CommonMark strips exactly one space from
+ * each end of a span, so the rendered text is unchanged.
+ */
+export function codeSpan(text: string): string {
+  const flat = text.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
+  if (flat === "") return "";
+
+  const longest = Math.max(0, ...(flat.match(/`+/g) ?? []).map((run) => run.length));
+  const ticks = "`".repeat(longest + 1);
+  const pad = flat.startsWith("`") || flat.endsWith("`") ? " " : "";
+
+  return `${ticks}${pad}${flat}${pad}${ticks}`;
+}

Progress note:
Fixed — a command containing backticks is now wrapped in a delimiter long enough to contain them, so it renders as one code span instead of closing at the first inner backtick.

## Before / after, using the exact command from your Paradev log

Before — the span closed at `` `bun run lint:fix` `` and the rest spilled into the cell as prose:

```
| 3 | s3 | `bun run lint # CI fails on warnings too. Run `bun run lint:fix` first. … | fail |
### s3 — `bun run lint # CI fails on warnings too. Run `bun run lint:fix` first. …`
```

After — the delimiter grows to two backticks, so the inner pair stays content:

```
| 1 | s1 | ``bun run lint # CI fails on warnings too. Run `bun run lint:fix` first.`` | fail |
### s1 — ``bun run lint # CI fails on warnings too. Run `bun run lint:fix` first.``
```

## What changed

- **[src/report.ts:91](src/report.ts#L91)** — new `codeSpan()`, the inline twin of the existing `fence()`: it measures the longest backtick run in the text and delimits with one tick more. When the content itself starts or ends with a backtick, it pads with a space at each end so that backtick cannot merge into the delimiter; CommonMark strips exactly one space from each end, so nothing extra renders. It replaces the five hand-rolled `` ` ``${…}`` ` `` wraps: the Steps table, the Not run table, the CI table, the `- **Command:**` / `- **Attempted fix:**` lines, and the `### sN —` failure heading.
- **[src/report.ts:63](src/report.ts#L63)** — `code()` flattens, truncates and escapes pipes first, then calls `codeSpan()`, so the fence is chosen on the final text (a cut inside a backtick run still gets a fence wider than what remains). An empty command now yields an empty cell instead of a stray pair of backticks.
- **[src/ci.ts:639](src/ci.ts#L639)** — the `mismatch` note no longer puts commands in code spans. That note is prose that the report flattens and cuts at 200 characters, and a cut landing inside a span leaves the backtick open — the same breakage one layer down. The command already has its own column; the note now reads `docs: bun run lint (CONTRIBUTING.md) · CI: bun run lint:prose (.github/workflows/ci.yml)`.

## Verification

`npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` are clean. I drove the real `buildReport` with the Paradev command plus adversarial ones, then parsed the output the way a renderer would — a code span closes only at a run of equal length, and a table row splits on unescaped pipes:

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Paradev `CONTRIBUTING.md` command with `` `bun run lint:fix` `` inside | one span, full text intact, 7 cells |
| `curl … \| bash -c "echo \`uname\`"` (pipe **and** backticks) | one span, pipe preserved, 7 cells |
| command starting and ending with a backtick | renders exactly, via the padding rule |
| `echo ```triple``` ` | 4-tick delimiter, renders exactly |
| every prose line in the whole report | zero unclosed backtick runs |

The scratch verifier and its log are removed, so your working tree only has the source changes.

Two limitations worth stating plainly. First, I could not re-run Paradev live to show the real report end to end: the Docker daemon is down after the restart (`connect ENOENT //./pipe/docker_engine`), and I didn't want to launch Docker Desktop on your behalf — start it and `npm start -- https://github.com/ParadevAI/Paradev --mode contributor` will show the corrected rows. Second, this fix covers backticks only; a pipe inside a command is still escaped as `\|` outside table cells, so `- **Command:**` lines show `curl … \| bash` literally. That's a separate, pre-existing wart I left alone rather than widen this change.

| Check | Result |

So every Docker call fails, `npm start` included. The tester runs `pingDocker()` before it clones anything, which is why you got one clean line in ~1 second instead of a stack trace, and why no temp directory or container was left behind. That's the designed fail-fast path.

## Why the message names `docker_engine`

Your Docker CLI talks to `dockerDesktopLinuxEngine` (the `desktop-linux` context), but the message says `//./pipe/docker_engine`. That's because `dockerode` doesn't read Docker contexts — its transport, `docker-modem`, falls back to the legacy Windows pipe whenever `DOCKER_HOST` is unset ([modem.js:21-24](node_modules/docker-modem/lib/modem.js#L21)):

When Docker Desktop is up it publishes both pipes, which is why your earlier Paradev runs worked. The name in the error is just the hardcoded default, not your active context.
